messages.content: 你能使用lawsuit_search功能從加州的聖塔克拉拉檢索所有涉及實體“Google”的訴訟，然後再從加州的聖馬刁檢索涉及實體“Facebook”的訴訟嗎？

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Retrieve all lawsuits involving a particular entity from specified jurisdiction. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

county.description: The jurisdiction for the lawsuit search.

state.description: The state for the lawsuit search. Default is California.

message.reasoning: The user wants to use the lawsuit_search function twice: first for entity "Google" in Santa Clara County, California; second for entity "Facebook" in San Mateo County, California. The user says "你能使用lawsuit_search功能從加州的聖塔克拉拉檢索所有涉及實體“Google”的訴訟，然後再從加州的聖馬刁檢索涉及實體“Facebook”的訴訟嗎？" So we need to call the function twice. The function signature: lawsuit_search(entity: string, county: string, state?: string). The default state is California. So we can omit state. We need to call it twice. According to policy, we should not provide the function output directly to the user. We should call the function and then wait for the tool response. So we need to produce a function call. But we need to call it twice. The policy says we can only call one function at a time. So we need to call the function once, get the result, then call again. But we can't do that in a single assistant message. We need to produce a function call, wait for the tool response, then produce another function call. So we need to produce the first function call. Then after receiving the tool response, we produce the second function call. So we need to produce the first function call now.
